Theorem
[Fundamental Theorem of Riemannian Geometry] 1. ch5:5.10

Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold, possibly with boundary. There is a unique symmetric connection $ abla $ on $TM$ compatible with $g$. It is the Levi-Civita connection of $g$, also called the Riemannian connection when $g$ is positive definite.

Proof

\sketch Metric compatibility applied to cyclic permutations of $X,Y,Z$, then combined with symmetry, yields

egin{align} \langle abla _XY,Z angle & = frac 12 igl(X\langle Y,Z angle +Y\langle Z,X angle -Z\langle X,Y angle otag \ & \qquad -\langle Y,[X,Z] angle -\langle Z,[Y,X] angle +\langle X,[Z,Y] angle igr). ag {5.5} \end{align}

Nondegeneracy of $g$ makes this formula determine $ abla _XY$, proving uniqueness.

In a coordinate chart, (5.5) gives

egin{equation} \langle abla _{\partial _i}\partial _j,\partial _l angle = rac12(\partial _i\langle \partial _j,\partial _l angle +\partial _j\langle \partial _l,\partial _i angle -\partial _l\langle \partial _i,\partial _j angle ), ag {5.6} \end{equation}

hence

egin{equation} \Gamma ^m_{ij}g_{ml} = rac12(\partial _ig_{jl}+\partial _jg_{il}-\partial _lg_{ij}) ag {5.7} \end{equation}

and

egin{equation} \Gamma ^k_{ij} = rac12g^{kl}(\partial _ig_{jl}+\partial _jg_{il}-\partial _lg_{ij}). ag {5.8} \end{equation}

These coefficients define local connections that agree on overlaps by uniqueness. They are symmetric in $i,j$, and (5.7) implies

\[ \Gamma ^l_{ki}g_{lj}+\Gamma ^l_{kj}g_{il}=\partial _kg_{ij}, \]

so Proposition 1 gives metric compatibility.
